correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly derives the exact count ab of zero-eligible edges from the label-two support degrees in K_n, then shows via degree sums and a strict neighboring-even comparison that every optimum has matching support. Strict forward differences of the resulting quadratic give a unique optimal matching size. A factorial matching count gives all minima. The independent full-labeling enumeration up to six root vertices (including 14,348,907 labelings), the support exhaustive search up to seven root vertices, and the direct construction validator up to ten root vertices all matched the algebra and included outputs; those finite checks are corroboration, not the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 standard-parameter work treats enumeration complexity and minimal-function algorithms but not this graph family. The 2019 standard perfect-Roman article gives complexity and algorithms for other classes. The 2024 perfect edge Roman chapter on complete root graphs imposes the additional condition that the entire label sum around a zero is two, and therefore addresses a strictly narrower feasible class. Previously available ordinary-Roman results for triangular graphs allow a zero to have multiple neighboring twos and do not imply this exact perfect-Roman optimum or matching count. Searches and source comparisons uncovered no theorem implying the all-order statement, subject to the separately recorded access and historical-priority risks.

value.rationale: A motivated graph-class question for the standard exactly-one-defender fault-assignment model is resolved in full for the infinite triangular family. An exact global optimum of quadratic order, rigid matching-only two-label support, forced cut-shaped zero set and closed factorial optimum multiplicity all follow. This is not merely a small finite case, code certificate or routine substitution; the strict exclusion of every higher-degree defender support is the structural content. The boundary \(n\ge3\) and distinct stronger edge model are identified.
